candidates.workingClaim: January 2, 1492: On January 2, 1492, Ferdinand II and Isabella I, the first monarchs of a unified Spain, captured Granada, ending a centuries-long series of military campaigns on the Iberian Peninsula.
January 2, 1905: On January 2, 1905, during the Russo-Japanese War, Russian forces surrendered Port Arthur (later Lushun, China) to the Japanese.
January 2, 2004: On January 2, 2004, NASA's Stardust spacecraft collected dust grains from the comet Wild 2.
January 2, 1920: On January 2, 1920, in the Palmer Raids, thousands of people were arrested in more than 30 US cities, accused of being foreign anarchists, communists, or radical leftists.
January 3, 1892: On January 3, 1892, J.R.R. Tolkien, author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, was born.
January 3, 1959: On January 3, 1959, Alaska became the 49th state of the United States.
January 3, 2019: On January 3, 2019, China's Chang'e 4 spacecraft, carrying the Yutu-2 rover, landed on the far side of the Moon.
January 3, 1521: On January 3, 1521, Pope Leo X excommunicated Martin Luther.
January 3, 1777: On January 3, 1777, during the American Revolution, the Battle of Princeton was fought in New Jersey.
January 4, 1809: On January 4, 1809, Louis Braille, who developed the system of printing and writing for the blind that bears his name, was born near Paris.
January 4, 1948: On January 4, 1948, Burma, today called Myanmar, formally gained independence from Great Britain.
January 4, 2010: On January 4, 2010, the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, officially opened in Dubai.
January 4, 1960: On January 4, 1960, the novelist and playwright Albert Camus was killed in an automobile accident in France.
January 4, 1853: On January 4, 1853, Solomon Northup, a free Black man who had been kidnapped in Washington, D.C., and sold into slavery, legally obtained his freedom.
January 5, 1953: On January 5, 1953, Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot was staged for the first time, in Paris.
January 5, 1933: On January 5, 1933, construction began on the Golden Gate Bridge, which connects San Francisco with Marin county.
January 5, 2005: On January 5, 2005, the dwarf planet Eris was discovered in images taken two years earlier at Palomar Observatory.
January 5, 1914: On January 5, 1914, Henry Ford raised his workers' pay from $2.40 to $5.00 a day.
January 5, 1925: On January 5, 1925, Nellie Tayloe Ross took office in Wyoming, becoming the first woman governor in the United States.
January 6, 1941: On January 6, 1941, US President Franklin D. Roosevelt outlined his Four Freedoms in his State of the Union message.
January 6, 1540: On January 6, 1540, Henry VIII of England married Anne of Cleves, the fourth of his six wives.
January 6, 1950: On January 6, 1950, Great Britain announced its recognition of the People's Republic of China.
January 6, 1838: On January 6, 1838, the composer Max Bruch was born in Cologne, in what is today Germany.
January 6, 1367: On January 6, 1367, the future King Richard II of England was born. He reigned from 1377 to 1399.
January 7, 1955: On January 7, 1955, the American contralto Marian Anderson first performed with the Metropolitan Opera in New York City.
January 7, 1979: On January 7, 1979, Vietnamese forces took control of Phnom Penh, Cambodia, removing the Khmer Rouge and Pol Pot from power.
January 7, 1968: On January 7, 1968, the uncrewed US space probe Surveyor 7 was launched; it went on to make a soft landing on the Moon.
January 7, 2003: On January 7, 2003, Christmas was celebrated as a national holiday in Egypt for the first time.
January 7, 2001: On January 7, 2001, John Kufuor was inaugurated as president of Ghana in the country's first peaceful transition of government.
January 8, 1912: On January 8, 1912, the African National Congress was founded in South Africa.
January 8, 1918: On January 8, 1918, US President Woodrow Wilson announced his Fourteen Points, a program for peace after World War I.
January 8, 1959: On January 8, 1959, Charles de Gaulle was inaugurated as president of France's Fifth Republic.
January 8, 1942: On January 8, 1942, the physicist Stephen Hawking was born. He developed a theory of exploding black holes.
January 8, 1935: On January 8, 1935, Elvis Presley, widely known as the King of Rock and Roll, was born.
